 Appearance:
 Ms. Durgesh Gupta - Advocate for appellant.
 Shri Amit Pandey - Government Advocate for State.
 Judgment

Per: Justice Vishal Dhagat Appellant had filed Criminal Appeal under Section 374(2) of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 challenging judgment and sentence dated 09/01/2016 passed by II Additional Sessions Judge, Hoshangabad in Sessions Trial No.360/2013.
2. Counsel appearing for appellant submitted that according to prosecution story on 01/10/2013 at about 02:00 P.M. appellant entered into house of prosecutrix and outrage her modesty.

Younger sister of prosecutrix came there and started crying, due to said reason appellant left the house threatening prosecutrix that he will kill her and defame her if she told the incident to any other person.
Written report (Ex.P-10) was lodged.

Police started investigation and filed its final charge-sheet under Section 452, 354, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:64347 2 CRA-578-2016 506, 323, 376 of IPC read with Section 4, 6, 8 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (in short 'POCSO Act, 2012).

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. Prosecution examined 14 witnesses to prove its case and appellant examined one defence witness in his favour.

Trial Court after considering entire prosecution evidence and deposition of witnesses had convicted appellant under Section 450, 323, 376(2)(i), 506(Part-II) of IPC and Section 8 of the POCSO Act, 2012 and sentenced him to undergo R.I. for eight years with fine of Rs.500/-, R.I. for 10 Rakesh Alias Kallu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185052177/
1 months, R.I. for 15 years with fine of Rs.1,000/-, R.I. for three years and R.I. for four years with fine of Rs.300/- respectively with default stipulation.
4.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Counsel appearing for appellant submitted that conviction and sentence of appellant is bad in law and finding given by trial Court is perverse.
It was submitted that Dr. Mohini Gupta (PW-2) has stated that there was no external or internal injury on the body of prosecutrix.
Prosecutrix is habitual to sexual intercourse and no definite opinion was given regarding commission of rape recently.
Trial Court further failed to see that there was no allegation of rape made by prosecutrix in FIR and in her statement.
Only allegation made was touching breast of prosecutrix.
Rekha Bai (PW-8) mother of prosecutrix has not supported the case of prosecution.
It was also argued that prosecutrix was not minor at the time of incident.
Prosecution failed to conduct Radiological examination.
Parents of prosecutrix do not know her actual date of birth.

It is submitted that date of birth was recorded on previous transfer certificate and no documents were produced before Teacher for recording date of birth of prosecutrix to be NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:64347 3 CRA-578-2016 10/10/1997.
Previous transfer certificate was not proved, nor source of previous date of birth was proved.
In these circumstances trial Court ought to have held that prosecution failed to prove that prosecutrix was minor.

It is also submitted that FSL report is negative and human sperms were not found on Article A, B and C, which are slides prepared from prosecutrix's pubic hair and her underwear, which is available on record as Ex.P-21 and witness Mohd. Shahjad Khan (PW-14)
was examined in respect of same.
Aforesaid circumstance shows that appellant was innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
It is prayed that appeal be allowed and appellant be acquitted.
5. Government Advocate appearing for State supported the judgment passed by trial Court.
It is submitted that prosecutrix, who had deposed in Court against appellant could not be disbelieved.
Negative report of MLC is of little or no consequences.
Prosecutrix has changed her clothes repeatedly and examination has also been done after delay.
Version of prosecutrix cannot be disbelieved.
Prosecution has proved that prosecutrix is below 16 years of age.
There is no infirmity or illegality in the judgment passed by trial Court.
In these circumstances appeal be dismissed.
6. Heard counsel appearing for parties.
Perused the record and deposition of witnesses.
7. FIR of case is Ex.P-10 and statement of prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. is Ex.P-12.
FIR was lodged on 02/10/2013 at about 05:45 P.M. of incident which occurred on 01/10/2013 at 02:00 P.M.
There is delay of more than 24 hours in lodging of FIR.
In FIR it has not been stated NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:64347 4 CRA-578-2016 that appellant committed rape on prosecutrix.
Statement of prosecutrix under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. was recorded on 19/10/2013.
In said statement she has stated that appellant committed rape on her.
He also threatened prosecutrix for not disclosing incident.

When prosecutrix and her sister started crying,
he ran away from house from back lane.
Appellant had also written letters to prosecutrix, in which appellant had repeatedly threated her.
Police has examined said letters through expert and it was found that letters were written by accused to her and his handwriting was found to be proved.

sentences.text: Prosecution has proved date of birth of prosecutrix to be 10/10/1997 as mentioned in Register (Ex.P-1).
She was admitted in school on 01/07/2008 and was granted T.C. on 15/04/2011.

On basis of entry made in admission register certificate has been issued by Head Master of School, which is Ex.P-2, wherein it has been stated that on basis of entry No.961 date of birth of prosecutrix is 10/10/1997.
Since offence in the instant case was allegedly committed on 01.10.2013, Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (J.J. Act) is not applicable.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 (J.J. Act)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Instead, Rule 12 of The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Rules, 2007 (Rules of 2007) will be applicable.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Rules, 2007 (Rules of 2007)
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The relevant portion of said Rule reads as under:-
"12. Procedure to be followed in determination of age.

- (1) In every case concerning a child or a juvenile in conflict with law, the court or the Board or as the case may be the Committee referred to in rule 19 of these rules shall determine the age of such juvenile or child or a juvenile in conflict with law within a period of thirty days from the date of making of the application for that NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:64347 5 CRA-578-2016 purpose.

(2) The court or the Board or as the case may be the Committee shall decide the juvenility or otherwise of the juvenile or the child or as the case may be the juvenile in conflict with law, prima facie on the basis of physical appearance or documents, if available, and send him to the observation home or in jail.
The prosecution has relied upon the admission register.

The Apex NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:64347 6 CRA-578-2016 Court in the case of Birad Mal Singhvi v. Anand Purohit Rakesh Alias Kallu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185052177/
3 1988 SCC (Supp.) 6 0 4 : provides that "The entries regarding dates of birth contained in scholar's register have no probative value, if no person on whose information the date of birth of the candidate was mentioned in the school record, is examined.

entities.text: Birad Mal Singhvi v. Anand Purohit Rakesh Alias Kallu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The entry contained in the admission form or in the scholar's register must be shown to be made on the basis of information given by the parents or a person having special knowledge about the date of birth of the person concerned.
The admission register cannot be relied upon as no evidence was placed before the Court to show on whose information this date of birth was recorded in the document.
Head Master Shyam Sundar Dubey (PW-1) was examined in Court.
Said witness stated that he has not seen any other document for making date of birth certificate except admission register.
Admission register was not prepared by him.
Prosecutrix was not examined by any Radiologist regarding her age.
Mother of prosecutrix has stated age of prosecutrix to be 17 years.
Said witness did not know her age.
She was unable to tell the date of birth of her all daughters and says that she was probably borne in year 1998.
She also stated that she has not given any document to policy showing age of prosecutrix.
She has denied suggestion that her daughter is more than 18 years of age.
10. On going through aforesaid evidence which is available on record it is found that prosecution has failed to prove date of birth of prosecutrix to be 10/10/1997.
Shyam Sundar Dubey (PW-1), who was examined to prove date of birth could not tell that on basis of which document date of birth 10/10/1997 was recorded in admission register.

No ossification test of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:64347 7 CRA-578-2016 prosecutrix was conducted.
Father, Mother and prosecutrix herself told age of prosecutrix to be 17 years.
Prosecution failed to show that prosecutrix was minor and was less then 16 years of age at the time of commission of offence.
11. Another question before this Court is whether on 01/10/2013 prosecutrix was raped by appellant or not.
Prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. stated that appellant had committed rape on her.
Prosecutrix (PW-9) had identified appellant in Court.
It was stated that he came to house on 01/10/2013 when she was alone in house.
However, she has not stated that appellant committed rape on her on said date.
She has stated that appellant used to threw letters in courtyard and said letters were proved by prosecution to have been written by appellant.
In Para-6 of cross-examination she stated that accused only teased her and threatened her.
In para-7 of cross-examination she stated that appellant committed bad act with her.
She had admitted that she had not told police that appellant had raped her.
But she had told said fact to Magistrate.
She has not told Doctor Mohini Gupta (PW-2) that she was raped.
She only told that she had changed her cloths many times.
Doctor also admitted that prosecutrix was habitual to sexual intercourse.
It was also not clear whether prosecutrix was wearing same underwear on date of examination, which she was wearing at the time of alleged incident.
In letters which were handed over to police it was found that appellant was threatening prosecutrix and he also stated that he has made videos of intimate relationship between them.
He was threatening her not to disclose the incident to any other person

,
otherwise he NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:64347 8 CRA-578-2016 will defame her.
He also forced her to marry him.
He has also stated that he had given her tables when her menses stopped and said tables were very costly.
He also threatened to beat her.
Prosecutrix has stated that appellant had committed rape on her.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From aforesaid evidence available on record, it is found that appellant had committed rape on prosecutrix many times.
On 01/10/2013 appellant had entered house, but may not commit rape on her.
Appellant had admitted that many times he committed sexual intercourse with prosecutrix and said fact is evident in his letters written to prosecutrix.
Pre MLC was negative and FSL report is also negative.
Said reports are inconsequential as appellant has repeatedly committed rape on prosecutrix on other occasions.
FSL was negative as Doctor has stated in deposition that prosecutrix has changed her undergarments many times before her examination.
Pre MLC took place after longtime, therefore, sperm were not found on Article A, B & C and same is inconsequential.
13. On basis of aforesaid evidence available on record trial Court has rightly held that prosecutrix was raped by appellant.
Trial Court had committed error in holding that on date of incident prosecutrix was minor.
Conviction of appellant under Section 8 of POCSO Act, 2012 is found to be bad in law, therefore, conviction of appellant under Section 8 of POCSO Act, 2012 is set aside.

14. Sentence under Section 376(2)(i) of IPC is also found tobe bad in law as prosecution has failed to prove beyond doubt that prosecutrix was less than 16 years of age at the time of incident, therefore,
conviction of appellant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:64347 9 CRA-578-2016 under Section 376(2)(i) of IPC is set aside.
15.

Appellant is convicted under Section 376(2)(n) of IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.1,000/- and in default of payment of fine, he has to undergo R.I. for further four months.
Conviction and sentence under Section 450, 323, 506 (Part-II) of IPC is maintained.
All sentences to run concurrently.
16. Superintendent of concerned jail is directed to calculate the period of custody of appellant and if appellant has completed 10 years of imprisonment, then he may be released from jail.
17. In view of above, appeal is disposed of.

(VISHAL DHAGAT) (B.
